headline: Wednesday's rally reversed: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% into a correction on AI-regulation fears, and December hike odds slipped to about two-thirds.
regime: Hiking regime with a volatility spike: the Fed raised rates in September, CME FedWatch puts the odds of another 25bp hike on Dec 9 at roughly two-thirds (down from the low 80s), and the VIX jumped to 28 on Thursday. In this regime good economic news can be bad for stocks, and yields matter more than usual.

lean.t: Rebound attempt in a shaky tape
lean.why: Futures point to a Nasdaq bounce (+1.17%) after a 5.5% drop, but the Dow is lower and the VIX is 26. The jobs report at 8:30 ET is the first test. Trade small.
CPI on Nov 10 and earnings from Rocket Lab, Constellation and Nebius come inside the window. The Nasdaq is in a correction and hike odds near two-thirds keep rates in focus.

Prices are lower after the drop, but AI spending now faces political scrutiny, and the Fed may still be hiking. Quality names with real earnings (Lilly grew revenue 38.6%) held up better than speculative groups.

rates.n: Held Oct 28, 10-2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike. Next meeting Dec 8-9
CME FedWatch about two-thirds (CappNotes, Nov 5), above 65% (Yahoo, Nov 6); down from the low 80s
Freddie Mac survey of Nov 5, down from 7.24%; third straight decline
Closed 28.18 on Nov 5, up about 70% (biggest jump since April 2025); 26.07 premarket Nov 6

sectors.why: (Nov 4 read, not updated Nov 6.) Democratic control keeps federal clean-energy support alive. First Solar rose 4.63% on Nov 4. Gridlock caps new laws, and spikes like this often give back some of the gain.
Health care fell 2.50% on Thursday after a record run Wednesday. Lilly beat (revenue +38.6%) but the group sold off with the market.
(Nov 4 read, not updated Nov 6.) Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%; GD, Northrop and RTX also fell. Defense budgets have usually been bipartisan, so deep cuts are less likely than headlines suggest.

Tech fell 8.0%, the semiconductor index more than 12%. Nvidia -9.3%, Micron -17.5%, AMD -17.3%. Premarket Nov 6 chips bounced 5% to 8.3%. The cause is fear of AI regulation and a slower data-center buildout.
Financials fell 2.87% on Thursday after a record on Wednesday. Higher rates help margins, but a growth scare and a possible jobs miss add credit worries.
The 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.18% (third weekly drop) and the 10-year is 4.84%. Rates are still about a point above last year.
Gold is about $4,098 (CappNotes) or $4,076 (Reuters), so it did not clearly rise in the selloff. A firmer dollar and hike odds are headwinds.
Energy fell 2.98% on Thursday with no advancers, even as WTI rebounded 2.7% to $90.52 after Wednesday's 8% drop.
The Russell 2000 fell 4.45% to 2,729.89. Small caps borrow short and are hurt when hike odds stay high.
Tesla fell 10.77% to $343.69 and SpaceX (SPCX) 9.05% to $123.62 on Thursday. One report ties the SpaceX drop to Musk spending about $0.5B backing GOP candidates.
Utilities fell 0.71% and real estate 1.82%, holding up better than the market, though falling yields help them.
(Nov 4 read, not updated Nov 6.) GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2%. Both had rallied on the immigration crackdown that a new Congress could oversee.

news.head: Stocks crash: S&P 500 -4.36%, Nasdaq -5.52% into a correction, worst day since April 2025
news.mean: The Dow fell 1,833 points (-3.44%) to 51,523, the S&P 500 lost 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, a correction from its Oct 6 record. About $3T of S&P value was lost on volume of 26.9B shares vs a 17.7B 20-day average. Only 71 S&P stocks advanced vs 431 decliners. Wednesday had been the Dow's best day since April 2025.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day drops are often followed by large swings in both directions, so a bounce on its own does not signal the low.
news.today: Volatility is high after a 4% index drop. Expect wide ranges around the 8:30 ET jobs report; keep size small.
news.later: Corrections that start from a policy scare are hard to time. Staging purchases, as some writers suggest for AI names, limits timing risk.

news.head: AI chips collapse: Nvidia -9.3%, Micron -17.5%, AMD -17.3%; chips bounce 5-8% premarket
news.srcN: CappNotes, Nov 5; Stock Titan, Nov 5; Yahoo Finance, Nov 6
news.mean: Tech fell 8.0%, the worst sector, and the semiconductor index lost more than 12%. Nvidia closed at $181.60 (-9.26%), Micron $656.39 (-17.46%), AMD $404.40 (-17.26%), Marvell $133.55 (-16.43%), Broadcom $291.53 (-10.43%) and Intel $52.25 (-10.33%). Qualcomm fell 9.49% to $156.75 on handset weakness. Premarket on Nov 6, Nvidia was up 3.6% and AMD, Intel, Broadcom and Micron up 5% to 8.3%.
news.today: The premarket bounce is a trading setup, not a trend. Watch whether it holds after the jobs release.
news.later: Data-center spending plans, not chip demand data, drove this fall. Earnings from Nebius (Nov 12) and Applied Materials will show if orders changed.

news.head: Midterm result drives AI-regulation fears: Democrats win Congress, data-center buildout in question
news.mean: Reuters ties the selloff to Democrats winning Congress, including in states where voters oppose data centers, which raised fears of AI regulation and a slower buildout. Argent's Jed Ellerbroek called it a "capitulation phase" for data-center capex beneficiaries. Reuters also notes a divided Washington could mean fewer sharp legislative changes but harder spending deals.
react: Power and cooling for data centers
news.today: Headlines on state data-center rules can move the group in minutes.
news.later: Gridlock usually slows big new laws. The practical risk is state-level permits and power rules rather than federal action.

news.head: Fed: December hike odds slip to about two-thirds as Hammack and Barkin hint at more hikes
news.srcN: Star-Advertiser (Reuters), Nov 5; CappNotes, Nov 5; Yahoo Finance, Nov 6
news.mean: CME FedWatch shows roughly a two-thirds chance (above 65%) of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting, down from the low 80s a day earlier. Reuters says Hammack and Barkin hinted at possible further hikes on Thursday. The Fed raised in September to 3.75-4.00% and held Oct 28.
react: Hike odds keep mortgage rates high
news.today: The jobs report at 8:30 ET is the next input for hike odds; a hot number would lift them again.
news.later: If the market selloff and a softer labor market cut hike odds further, rate-sensitive groups tend to benefit first.

news.head: October jobs report today: consensus +65k, unemployment 4.2%
news.mean: Consensus is about +65,000 payrolls with unemployment at 4.2%, per CappNotes. September payrolls were +29,000. Continuum Economics, whose own forecast is +50,000, expects wages up 0.2% m/m and 2.8% y/y. Jobless claims on Nov 5 were 189,000, the lowest since mid-July, vs about 196,000 expected.
react: Strong jobs help margins, weak jobs hurt credit
Gold reacts to yields and the dollar
news.today: Trade the reaction to the 8:30 ET release, not the number alone; compare it with the 65k consensus.
news.later: One report rarely changes the trend. CPI on Nov 10 is the bigger input to a December hike.

news.head: Treasury yields fall: 10-year 4.84%, near a two-month low
news.mean: CappNotes has the 10-year at 4.84% (-6bp), the 30-year at 5.25% and the 2-year at 4.46%; Reuters shows 4.86% and 5.28%. The 2s10s spread is about 38bp. The dollar index was about 101.60 (Reuters 101.87). Bonds were bid as stocks sold off.
news.today: A fall in yields on a risk-off day does not always last once stocks stabilize.
news.later: A 10-year back below 4.5% is the level that would ease housing and small-cap pressure.

news.head: Mortgage rates fall for a third week to 7.18%
news.mean: The 30-year fixed averaged 7.18%, down from 7.24% last week and up from 6.22% a year ago. The 15-year averaged 6.57%, down from 6.60% (5.50% a year ago). Freddie Mac's Sam Khater said rates "continued their downward trajectory" this week.
news.today: Housing stocks follow the 10-year more than the weekly survey.
news.later: Rates are still nearly a full point above a year ago, so demand relief is slow.

news.head: Oil rebounds after an 8% drop: WTI $90.52 (+2.7%), Brent $98.29 (+3.8%)
news.mean: WTI settled at $90.52 and Brent at $98.29, both rebounding after falling about 8% on Wednesday. Reuters says the Middle East conflict is keeping oil and inflation elevated. Energy stocks still fell 2.98% on Thursday, with zero advancers in the sector.
react: Sector fell despite the oil rebound
news.today: Oil has been headline-driven this week. Use wide stops or stand aside.
news.later: Oil above $90 keeps headline inflation elevated and complicates the Fed's path.

news.head: Gold near $4,100 and silver about $51.84 as stocks sell off
news.mean: CappNotes has gold at about $4,098 (+0.61%) and silver at $51.84; Reuters shows gold at $4,076.25 (-0.91%), so sources differ on direction. Bitcoin fell 5.7% to about $75,855. The dollar index was about 101.6.
react: Gold did not act as a clear haven
news.today: Gold and stocks both fell in the Reuters data, which suggests selling for cash rather than a flight to safety.
news.later: Hawkish Fed talk and a firmer dollar are the main headwinds for gold.

news.head: Bank of England hikes to 4.00%; Banxico cuts to 6.25%
news.mean: The Bank of England raised its Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00% from 3.75%, in line with consensus, on an 8-1 vote. Banxico cut 25bp to 6.25% vs 6.50% expected.
news.today: A hike that matched expectations usually moves the currency less than the vote split or guidance.
news.later: Another central bank hiking supports the view that the Fed is not alone in tightening.

news.head: Earnings: Cloudflare +17%, Airbnb +12%, Atlassian -16%, DraftKings -18%; AppLovin +31% on Thursday
news.mean: AppLovin closed +31% on Thursday (EPS $4.30 vs $4.04) on a day the Nasdaq fell 5.5%. After hours, Cloudflare rose about 17% (EPS $0.38 vs $0.34, revenue $782.5M vs $736.8M, raised outlook), and Airbnb was up 12.1% premarket (EPS $3.16 vs $2.85). Atlassian fell about 15.6% on a cautious cloud outlook and DraftKings about 18% on a miss and lower guidance. Axon fell about 14% and Five9 about 18%.
news.today: Strong results are rewarded even in a selloff; weak guidance is punished hard.
news.later: Companies that beat and raise in a falling market are the ones that tend to recover first.

news.head: Futures rebound before the open: Nasdaq +1.17%, S&P +0.20%, Dow -0.89%; VIX 26
news.mean: Premarket, S&P futures were up 0.20%, Nasdaq futures up 1.17% and Dow futures down 0.89%. The VIX was 26.07 after closing at 28.18 on Thursday. Kospi fell 5.28% and the Nikkei 1.79% on Thursday, while the Hang Seng rose 3.67%.
news.today: The open and the 8:30 ET jobs data are the two tests of the bounce.
news.later: A bounce after a 4% drop is not a bottom signal by itself; breadth and volume need to recover.

calendar.usual: Consensus +65k, 4.2% (September was +29k). Big moves in yields, the dollar and banks.

calendar.t: Constellation Energy and Rocket Lab earnings
calendar.usual: Tests the data-center power and space themes after the Nov 5 drop.
The key input to December's hike. Core matters more than the headline.

scen.title: What if today's jobs number is...

out: Mixed to lower; growth and small caps worst
Relief; focus moves to CPI Nov 10
Growth and small caps rally, unless recession fear takes over

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
